canonical_question: Does the '10 nm diameter' of sub-cascades observed in simulations directly correlate to the initial grain size of this specific W-Ta-Cr-V-Hf alloy, and what is that grain size?

question_variants.question: Does the '10 nm diameter' of sub-cascades observed in simulations directly correlate to the initial grain size of this specific W-Ta-Cr-V-Hf alloy, and what is that grain size?
question_variants.resolution_summary: The text states that the sub-cascade diameter (10 nm) is 'near the initial grain-size', implying a correlation, but it does not provide the specific numerical value of the initial grain size for the W-Ta-Cr-V-Hf alloy. It only provides the simulation-derived sub-cascade limit.

answers.answer: The text notes a correlation where the 10 nm sub-cascade diameter is near the initial grain size, but does not explicitly state the numerical grain size value. The evidence states: 'Molecular dynamics simulations have shown that high-energy (50 keV) recoil events begin to divide in sub-cascades [34] , [35] , each with a diameter on the order of 10 nm. This upper limit on cascade size is near the initial grain-size'.
answers.mechanism: cascade size near initial grain size
answers.boundary_limitation: Initial grain size value not explicitly stated in text
evidence_spans: The results here demonstrate that grain refinement only occurred when the heavy ions are introduced.
This suggests that such a grain refinement observed in the dual-beam irradiation case was caused by a cascade effect.
The in situ nature of the experiments performed in this work has allowed us to observe the grain refinement effect in real-time
